chapter: Career overview and the Lunceford quarrel
title: Mary Lou Williams sends him to Cafe Society and Ed Hall
summary: After the Army, Mary Lou Williams steers him past the 802 union problem to a job with Ed Hall's group at Cafe Society, where he had peeked at the drummer.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: And after I got out of the Army, in the meantime, Lunceford they wouldn't let nobody in Lunceford's band -- join Musician's Local #802. They were trying to break it up. And a colored guy was behind it, Peekaboo. And so, when I got out of the Army, by chance I went to the Union #802, and I ran into Mary Lou Williams, who I knew well in Memphis. And she asked me what was I doing. I says, darling, I'm not doing anything. I'm just -- I just got discharged from the Army. She say, you want a job? I say, oh, God; thank you. I certainly do. I need one.

May be going a little ahead of you, but this was 1945, when I -- I got out of the Army in 1941 five. I went in in '43. So she said, all right. Ponder me (Inaudible). She said, come down to Cafe Society --that's when it was uptown -- and talk with Ed Hall, clarinetist (Inaudible). So, boy, I was afraid because I never played with nothing but big bands, you know, like Lunceford's. And I used to go down there every night, peek -- find me a crack -- I used to peek through at the drummer and see what he was doing and how he was cutting it.

But Mary Lou Williams for some reason couldn't stand (Arthur) Trappier this fellow. Shapiro was his name. And so she had me to come and speak to Ed Hall. Sure enough, I did, and so I got a job there, did all right, did quite well. I'm very proud of myself. Perseverance is a great thing. When you're hungry --

oh, you -- I was with that little girl there, my wife, [Irene] Crawford. I used to go down there every night and peek through that crack, standing on the outside, looking in, cold, wet, rain, anything. I just wanted to see what the drummer was doing. He was cutting a show, fast hands.

So I got in Cafe Society with Ed Hall, stayed with Ed Hall for over three years. I was very good. And so they have another Cafe Society downtown, down in the Village, number 1, Sheridan Square, I think the number was. I stayed with Ed Hall for over three years, beautiful person to work for, just beautiful.
